summary: The archive: store, first build and syncs, analytics, periods, chart formatting and exports.

src/archive/exports.js.note: fileStem, exportArchive, exportPosts and exportRows are ported and held to the fixture (the text, name and type each download hands over). downloadText's browser plumbing (a Blob URL, an anchor's click, the revoke timer) is the UI's: here it returns an ExportFile, which VirgaUI saves or shares with fileExporter or ShareLink.

src/archive/postChanges.js.note: Ported in full. applyPostChanges compares a row's lists (tags, links, mentions, langs) by value where the web's !== compares them by reference, so a held row noted again with equal but separate lists reads as unchanged here and changed on the web; the rows that come back are the same either way. Swift returns nil for 'unchanged' (the web returns the same array).

src/lib/analyticsExport.js.note: Ported in full. archiveJson writes the document's own members in the web's order (held by the fixture's key list); inside a row or the meta, members are written sorted, where the web keeps each object's insertion order. A reader can't tell the difference.

src/lib/analyticsStore.js.note: IndexedDB is VirgaCore's FileStore here: one database per DID under analytics/<encodeURIComponent(name)>/, its schema (version 1, the same stores and key paths) in schema.json, each write a segment replayed in order, rows as the web's JSON, read back in IndexedDB's key order (numbers, then strings by code unit; the memory fallback keeps first-write order as the web's Map does). A database above version 1 is served from memory, as a VersionError open is on the web. The blocked-by-another-tab wait (BLOCKED_WAIT_MS, onblocked, onversionchange) has no iOS case: nothing else opens the files; blocked is always false. deleteDatabase(name, files:) stands in for indexedDB.deleteDatabase and closes an open handle as onversionchange does. Keys other than strings and numbers (dates, arrays, binary) are skipped.
